defs: said something in an angry or mean way
spoke in a sharp, cross voice to someone
said words quickly in an unkind, grumpy way
exs: Mom snapped at us when we were too loud.
The tired teacher snapped at the noisy class.
"Leave me alone!" he snapped at his little sister.

defs: in a way that looks like you did nothing wrong
in a way that acts as if you did no wrong
with a sweet, quiet look that hides a secret
exs: She smiled innocently, but she ate the cake.
The puppy looked up innocently with the sock in his mouth.
"I didn't see anything," said Tom innocently.

defs: looks like or seems
seems to be true from what you see
comes into view; shows up
exs: It appears that it will rain soon.
The sky is dark, so it appears that a storm is coming.
A rainbow appears after the rain stops.

defs: a dirty or untidy place or thing
a place where things are not in order
a pile of things left all over the floor
exs: Please clean up the mess.
My room is such a mess after the party.
The baby made a big mess with his food.

defs: a sweet drink made from lemons
a cold yellow drink made with lemon juice and sugar
a sour and sweet drink you can sell at a stand
exs: We sold cold lemonade on the street.
On hot days, we drink cold lemonade with ice.
Grandma made a jug of fresh lemonade for the picnic.

defs: not smart (a rude word, so do not say it to people)
not clever; a rude word for silly
silly or not wise, but not a nice thing to say
exs: That was a dumb mistake.
I felt dumb when I forgot my own name.
It was a dumb idea to go out without a coat.

defs: things that you do
the things a person does, not what they say
deeds or acts that show how you behave
exs: Your actions show that you are kind.
Helping the old man was one of his kind actions.
We learn from our mistakes and our actions.

defs: to say that you are not happy about something
to tell others that something is bad or unfair
to grumble because you are not pleased
exs: Please don't complain about the food.
Don't complain when the soup is a little hot.
My brother likes to complain about his homework.

defs: to bring things to people or places
to carry something to the place it must go
to take packages or letters to someone's door
exs: He will deliver the mail every morning.
The milkman will deliver milk to our house.
Can you deliver this note to the teacher?

defs: spoke quietly and not clearly, almost to yourself
talked in a low voice that is hard to hear
said words softly so nobody could understand well
exs: He mumbled that he was sorry.
Ben mumbled his answer, so nobody could hear him.
She mumbled to herself while she looked for her shoes.

defs: in a clean and tidy way
in an orderly way with everything in its place
carefully, without any mess
exs: She folded her clothes neatly.
He wrote his name neatly at the top of the page.
The books were stacked neatly on the shelf.

defs: able to wait without getting angry
calm when you must wait a long time
not angry or upset when things are slow
exs: Be patient. Your turn is coming.
The patient fisherman waited all day for one fish.
You must be patient when you learn to ride a bike.

defs: to show that something is true
to give facts that show something is real
to show everyone that you are right
exs: Can you prove it?
I can prove that I finished my homework.
The footprints prove that a fox was here.

defs: confused
not able to understand something
mixed up and unsure what is going on
exs: I was puzzled by the hard question.
Mia looked puzzled when she saw the empty box.
The puzzled boy scratched his head at the strange map.

defs: the way you go from one place to another
the road or path you take on a trip
the streets that a driver follows each day
exs: The bus route goes past our school.
Dad took a different route to avoid the traffic.
The paper boy knows his route by heart.

defs: thin stretchy rings that hold things together
stretchy loops that can hold papers or hair
little elastic circles you can wrap around a bunch of things
exs: Put rubber bands around the pencils.
She tied her hair with colorful rubber bands.
I shot paper balls with rubber bands in art class.

defs: to disappear
to go away and not be seen anymore
to suddenly be gone, as if by magic
exs: The magician made the coin vanish.
The snowman will vanish when the sun comes out.
I watched the rabbit vanish into the hole.

defs: to tell everyone something
to say something loudly so all can hear
to make news known to a group
exs: The teacher will announce the winner.
The principal will announce the field trip today.
Dad wanted to announce that we are getting a puppy.

defs: to take care of a child while the parents are out
to look after young kids for money while adults are away
to watch a small child when the parents go out
exs: I baby-sit my little cousin on Sundays.
Mrs. Lee asked Anna to baby-sit her twin boys.
My big sister will baby-sit me tonight.

defs: a small bowl of water for birds
a shallow dish in a garden where birds drink
a stone bowl filled with water for little birds to splash in
exs: Birds splash in the birdbath.
A robin sat on the edge of the birdbath.
We fill the birdbath with fresh water every day.

defs: in a happy way
with a glad and cheerful feeling
in a joyful way, with a smile
exs: The kids played happily.
The puppy wagged its tail happily.
They sang happily on the way to the beach.

defs: stopped for a short time
stopped what you were doing for a moment
waited a little before going on
exs: He paused to take a breath.
She paused at the door and looked back.
The music paused, and then it started again.

defs: to act as if something is true when it is not
to make believe something is real in a game
to act like someone or something you are not
exs: Let's pretend we are pirates.
I like to pretend that my bed is a boat.
Don't pretend you are asleep, Sam!

defs: to give part of what you have to someone
to let others use or have part of your things
to divide something so that two people both get some
exs: I will share my snack with you.
Please share your crayons with the new girl.
The twins share a room at their grandma's house.

defs: to make something very wet
to put something in water until it is completely wet
to wet something all the way through
exs: The rain will soak my shoes.
Soak the dirty socks in the bucket for an hour.
The big wave will soak your towel.
